dossier.public_summary: The dips land on the target star but their depths alternate between odd and even eclipses and fall much shallower in one sector, with a brightness swing outside the dips comparable to the dips themselves. This pattern matches a grazing stellar companion eclipsed every 3 days and folded to 1.5 days around the active M dwarf, not a normal planet.

reasons.why: Alternating eclipse depths differ significantly, the classic signature of a binary at twice the folded period. Even fit log density ratio -2.47 shows shape mismatch, favouring stellar companion over planet.

Massive out-of-transit swing equal to the transit depth (phase_curve ratio 0.981) indicates reflected / ellipsoidal / beaming from a close binary, with variability_chi2_dof 265.3. Spot modulation on this M dwarf is huge (rotation amplitude 84786 ppm) but the equal amplitude-phase signal is binary-like, not spot-only.

Depth collapses by 81% in sector 73 with the same TESS-SPOC pipeline, so the dip is not steady. Odd transits alternate more deeply when counting even vs odd in sectors 20 and 73 (sector_oe_max_sigma 9.692), supporting a binary folded at half the true period.
reasons.value: p_constant 3.034e-12, sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source, depths 7033, 8157, 3176 ppm

reasons.why: On_target rules out the 21 nearby stars that could cause the dip, so the eclipses are on the target itself; flat shape.v_sigma -6.057 with b 0.840 grazes are still consistent with a small-star eclipse, and centroid_all confirms no blend.

Period is exactly the star's spot period by design, but the large phase-curve swing and sector 73 depth drop show the 1.5 d period is best explained as an eclipsing binary folded at P/2, not chance alignment of a planet with the rotation period.
